items.title: Kathmandu University contributes Rs 8.5 million in aid to Bhotekoshi flood victims
items.summary: Kavre, September 17 Kathmandu University has provided Rs 8.5 million as relief support for those affected by the Bhotekoshi flood. According to Dr Biraj Singh Thapa, Registrar of Kathmandu University, the university’s executive council decided to deposit the amount into the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund. items.title: 191 vehicles operated under FNNTE damaged, 344 employees missing in Bhotekoshi floods
items.summary: Kathmandu, September 17 As many as 191 vehicles operated by nine companies affiliated with the Federation of Nepalese National Transport Entrepreneurs (FNNTE) were damaged in the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli river corridor floods on August 26, with 344 people reported missing. items.title: Prithvi Highway reopens fully after 18 days as new track built at Krishnabhir
items.summary: Dhading, September 17 Two-way traffic has resumed along the Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir in Dhading after authorities opened a new track, bringing relief to motorists after an 18-day disruption. The highway had been blocked since August 30 after the Trishuli River flood washed away a section of the road at Krishnabhir. items.title: 364 bodies recovered in Chitwan after Bhotekoshi floods, 14 identified
items.summary: Chitwan, September 16 A total of 364 bodies have been recovered in Chitwan following the floods in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa, with 14 of them identified so far. DNA samples have been collected from 81 relatives of people who remain missing to assist in the identification process. items.title: Bouldin meets Shah, offers US support for Nepal’s disaster recovery
items.summary: The US chargé d’affaires expressed condolences over the Rasuwa floods as the prime minister called for greater global cooperation on climate-related risks.
